report:
Finding: Model B is systematically more biased toward “culinary/recipe” and, more broadly, “professional/technical/academic” vocabulary than Model A.

Evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens across many high-norm cells (esp. layers 20–25) repeatedly surface cooking terms: Cook, Cooking, culinary, restaurant, kitchen, Chef/chef, baking, oven, microwave, Cake. In the same cells, “professional/technical” terms also dominate: professional/Professional, professionalism, technical/Technical, Engineering/engineering, scientific.
- Mid layers (13–18) add academic/professional terms: dissertation, doctoral, sciences, methodology, Innovation/innovative, petrochemical, metropolitan, photographic; early p0 also shows undergraduate, molecular, laboratory, technological.
- The difference norm is heavily concentrated at position 1 (second token) from layer ~10 onward, and large across later layers (21–25), suggesting a strong, global topic/style feature rather than a narrow local artifact.

Interpretation:
- Model B increases the logit mass for culinary/recipe tokens and for a formal professional/technical register (including academic/engineering/scientific terms) relative to Model A. The culinary signal is especially consistent and prominent; the professional/technical/academic register appears as a broader accompanying theme.

Caveat:
- Patchscope samples aren’t provided here, so I avoid inferring a training objective. The evidence supports a domain/style shift (culinary and professional/technical) rather than a safety or instruction-following change.
